title: Hearing Calendar Terms of the Unemployment Insurance Appeals Dockets
content:
For **Unemployment Insurance Appeals**, the calendar terms below are fixed per docket: whether an evidentiary hearing is held at all, the mode a hearing is held in unless another is granted, whether a party may ask for an in-person hearing, the scheduling target (calendar days after filing within which the first hearing is set), the minimum calendar days between the mailing of a hearing notice and the hearing date, the time scheduled for the hearing, and the calendar days after filing within which written argument may be submitted. A value of 0 in the scheduling target, notice minimum or hearing length means that the docket holds no hearing; a value of 0 in written argument means that written argument is not applicable.

| Docket | Hearing held | Default mode | In-person on request | Scheduling target (calendar days) | Notice minimum (calendar days) | Hearing length (minutes) | Written argument (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue | yes | telephone | yes | 30 | 7 | 60 | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue | yes | telephone | yes | 21 | 7 | 45 | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination | yes | telephone | yes | 30 | 7 | 45 | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud | yes | telephone | yes | 30 | 7 | 60 | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge | yes | telephone | yes | 45 | 7 | 60 | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate | yes | telephone | yes | 60 | 7 | 90 | 0 |
| Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review | no (decided on the record) | record review | no | 0 | 0 | 0 | 14 |

**Delivery of notices.** On every docket, hearing notices and decisions are delivered by mail and in the online portal.

## Notes on the table

- The six lower-authority dockets all hold a telephone hearing by default and all admit a request for an in-person hearing; they differ in scheduling target (21 to 60 days) and hearing length (45 to 90 minutes).
- The Board of Review holds no hearing: its scheduling target, notice minimum and hearing length are all 0, and it accepts written argument within 14 calendar days after filing.
- Illustration: the longest hearing time is scheduled on the Employer Contribution Rate docket (90 minutes); the Able and Available Issue and Monetary Determination dockets are scheduled for 45 minutes; the Separation Issue, Overpayment and Fraud and Employer Benefit Charge dockets for 60 minutes.
